title: Debt: Unchecked thread creation in platform_thread (Win32)
description: platform_thread.h:97: pt_thread_create malloc for PT__ThreadArgs can fail without error handling. CreateThread at line 100 may also fail silently. If malloc fails, the freed pointer is still passed to CreateThread; if CreateThread fails, no error returned. Add null checks and return error status.
close_reason: pt_thread_create returns int; Win32 checks malloc'd arg and CreateThread, POSIX checks pthread_create; net_thread_start propagates failure.

title: Perf: Add render distance configuration (runtime flag or config)
description: User manually reduced render_distance from 32 to 8 chunks (src/main.c:281 uncomitted change). This is the single most impactful knob for iGPU: 32-chunk radius = ~3200 chunks in view, 8-chunk = ~200 chunks. Recommendation: Add --render-distance N command-line flag to main.c and runtime config. Store in World struct (already done). File: src/main.c:281 (hardcoded to 8, needs parameterization), src/world.c:273-280 (already supports parameter)

title: Perf: Disable 4x MSAA by default on iGPU (configurable)
description: 4x MSAA is extremely expensive on integrated GPUs. Currently hardcoded in renderer.c:798-800 to detect 4x support and enable it. Recommendation: Make MSAA configurable (environment var or config file), default to OFF on iGPU (detected via device properties), or add --no-msaa flag to main.c. Impact: 2-3x fill-rate savings on Mesa/Intel iGPU. File: src/renderer.c:798-800 (sample_count selection)

title: Debt: Silent allocation failures in net_thread
description: net_thread.c:16-17: malloc for NetMsg inside thread_func fails silently with 'if (!msg) continue;' — drops received packet without logging. Same at line 83. During high traffic, silent packet loss can accumulate. Add logging or consider preallocated pool. Also line 58: pt_thread_create return value discarded.
close_reason: Added atomic dropped-packet counter (inbound+outbound) with periodic stderr warning; queue semantics unchanged.

title: Debt: Unchecked Vulkan VkResult returns in renderer
description:
Several critical Vulkan calls ignore return values:
- renderer.c:775: vkCreateDebugUtilsMessengerEXT result not checked
- renderer.c:1206: vkAllocateCommandBuffers result not checked
- renderer_frame.c:31,51,78,83,213: vkWaitForFences, vkResetFences, vkResetCommandBuffer, vkBeginCommandBuffer, vkEndCommandBuffer return values not checked
- renderer_frame.c:258: vkQueuePresentKHR handles OOD/SUBOPTIMAL but may miss other errors
Add proper error handling to catch device lost / submission failures.
close_reason: Checked previously-ignored VkResult returns in renderer.c and renderer_frame.c; log+fail cleanly, DEVICE_LOST/out-of-date paths preserved.

title: Debt: Unchecked allocation returns in chunk_map, lighting, and block_physics
description:
Multiple malloc/calloc/realloc calls lack null checks:
- chunk_map.c:34,60: calloc returns not checked before use
- lighting.c:100,212,401-402: malloc for LightQueue can fail silently
- block_physics.c:56,74: malloc for keys array lacks error check
These can cause crash/corruption if allocation fails. Add null checks and error paths.
close_reason: Added calloc NULL checks (abort + stderr) in chunk_map_init and rehash; lighting.c and block_physics.c allocations were already checked.

title: Perf: Disable validation layers in Release builds and runtime
description: Validation layers are conditionally enabled in renderer.c:744-748 when NDEBUG is not set. If built in Debug mode, validation layer overhead is significant on iGPU. Recommendation: Ensure CMakeLists.txt uses Release mode by default with -O2/-O3. Also expose a runtime --no-validation flag or env var to bypass layer loading. File: src/renderer.c:744-748 (layer enablement), CMakeLists.txt (build type)

title: Perf: Verify frustum culling is effective (measure chunks culled)
description: Frustum culling is implemented in renderer_frame.c:143-154 using frustum_extract() and frustum_test_aabb(). Verify it's working: currently every chunk in world_get_meshes() calls frustum_test, but if radius is large, many off-screen chunks still submitted. Recommendation: Add debug logging to measure effective culling ratio. File: src/renderer_frame.c:153 (culling check), src/frustum.c (culling math)

title: Perf: Make anisotropic filtering configurable (default 1x on iGPU)
description: 16x anisotropic filtering is costly on iGPU bandwidth. Currently hardcoded in texture.c:276-288 to use maxSamplerAnisotropy (capped at 16.0f). Recommendation: Add config to allow disabling (aniso=1.0) or reducing (aniso=4.0 instead of 16.0) for iGPU. Detect iGPU and default to 1.0 (trilinear only) or 4.0. Impact: 5-10% bandwidth savings for memory-limited iGPU. File: src/texture.c:276-288 (sampler anisotropy setup)

title: Netcode: add protocol version field + connect handshake version check
description: Serialization is hand-rolled byte packing with NO version field (net.h header: type/player_id/seq/ack/ack_bits). A client/server packet-format mismatch corrupts silently. Add a protocol version constant, carry it in PKT_CONNECT_REQUEST/ACCEPT, and reject mismatched clients with a clear disconnect reason. FOUNDATION: land this before features add new packets so format drift is caught, not silently corrupting. Effort S.
close_reason: Implemented: protocol version + handshake rejection with typed disconnect reasons; net unit tests pass. On feat/netcode-version.

title: World persistence (save/load chunks to disk)
description: Worlds are seed-only and reset every session, including player block edits. Serialize modified chunks + player state to disk on the server and reload on startup. Enables base building.
close_reason: Implemented server-side world persistence: block-delta overlay (world_persist module) records every break/place, replays onto generated chunks, saves on shutdown + 30s flush, loads on startup. Pure serialize/deserialize roundtrip + file I/O unit-tested (test_world_persist, 7 cases). Full build clean, all 12 ctests pass. Branch feat/world-persistence.

title: Ores and minerals (coal/iron/gold/diamond) with depth-based worldgen
description: All stone is identical. Add ore block types and distribute them in worldgen by depth (coal common shallow, diamond rare deep) using deterministic noise so it is unit-testable. Foundation for crafting/tools progression.
close_reason: Implemented: 4 ore types, depth-based deterministic worldgen distribution, textures, unit tests (12/12 pass). Committed on feat/ores.

title: Day/night cycle with time-gated mob spawning
description: No time-of-day exists; lighting is static and mobs spawn at all times. Add a server-authoritative world time clock, broadcast it to clients, drive sky/sun brightness in the renderer, and gate hostile mob spawning to night/darkness. Foundational for atmosphere and survival pacing.

title: Perf: in-game FPS/frametime + visible-chunk counter (perf feedback)
description: Add a lightweight on-screen (and/or stdout every N sec) frametime + FPS readout, plus visible-chunk and draw-call counts, so the performance impact of changes is measurable on the user's integrated-GPU laptop. Toggle via a key or --stats flag. Enables before/after comparison of perf patches.

title: Villages: well + paths + terrain flattening
description: Add the central well (3x3 COBBLE rim, hollow WATER core, PLANKS corner posts + canopy), BLOCK_PATH paths connecting each house door to the well (Bresenham computed in WORLD coords, emitted per-block via chunk_set_block so paths split across chunk boundaries automatically), and terrain flattening under each building footprint to a shared platform Y derived from worldgen_get_height at the village/building center (pure, so identical in every chunk it spans): clear interior volume to AIR (removes intruding trees), fill DIRT below platform where ground dips, lay PLANKS/COBBLE floor at platform. Extend tests/test_village.c with the cross-chunk consistency test: generate two chunks straddling a village boundary and assert identical block stacks in the overlap. See docs/plans/villages.md sections 6,7,8,10.
close_reason: Central cobble/water well with plank posts + cobble canopy, Bresenham gravel PATH from each house door to the well, and footprint terrain flattening (clear-to-air above platform, dirt fill below). Emitted in world coords so pieces split across chunks automatically. Seam test asserts the 3x3 canopy reconstructs completely across chunk boundaries.

title: Villages: per-chunk building generation
description: Implement village_generate(Chunk* chunk, int seed, int height_map[CHUNK_X][CHUNK_Z]) in src/village.c and add the 1-2 line call site in src/worldgen.c (include village.h; call after the tree loop, before atomic_store(state)) to keep the worldgen.c footprint tiny for merge safety with the concurrent persistence work. Per-chunk intersection strategy: scan the 3x3 cell window around the chunk, village_cell_at + village_is_suitable (pure), AABB-reject against chunk, then deterministically derive house layout from vc.seed and emit every block in WORLD coords via chunk_set_block(chunk, wx-base_x, wy, wz-base_z, block). Out-of-[0,16) writes are silently dropped by chunk.h bounds checks, so each chunk renders only its slice with NO neighbor writes. House: PLANKS walls/floor, flat COBBLE or peaked PLANKS roof, GLASS window gaps, air door gap. Add src/village.c to the minecraft target in CMakeLists.txt. See docs/plans/villages.md sections 2,5,6.
close_reason: village_generate per-chunk intersection loop (3x3 cell scan, AABB reject, suitability via worldgen_get_height) emits houses via chunk_set_block in world coords; flatten platform, plank walls, door gaps, glass windows, flat/peaked roofs. Single-line call site added to worldgen_generate. Cross-chunk seam test passes.

title: Villages: deterministic cell placement + suitability (pure+tested)
description: Create new module src/village.h/.c with PURE, unit-testable placement logic modeled on src/ore.c. Add: village_cell_at(cgx,cgz,world_seed)->VillageCell{present,wx,wz,seed} using hash_pos-style mixing over a coarse cell grid (VILLAGE_CELL_CHUNKS=16, VILLAGE_SPAWN_PCT~25, center jittered inside cell with margin so adjacent cells can't overlap); and village_is_suitable(center_h,center_block,min_h,max_h) requiring center_h>=SEA_LEVEL+1, center_block==BLOCK_GRASS, and flatness max_h-min_h<=VILLAGE_MAX_SLOPE. Suitability is sampled via the pure worldgen_get_height so it is chunk-independent (crux of cross-chunk consistency). Add tests/test_village.c (deterministic, density sane, center in-bounds/non-overlap, suitability gating) and wire it in CMakeLists.txt next to test_ore (link src/village.c src/block.c, +m). See docs/plans/villages.md sections 4 and 8.
close_reason: Pure village_cell_at (deterministic placement + margin-clamped jitter) and village_is_suitable (sea level/grass/flatness) implemented in src/village.{c,h}; tests/test_village.c verifies determinism, density ~25%, center bounds, suitability gating. New CMake target 'village' wired like test_ore.

title: Villages: decorative blocks (planks/cobblestone/glass/path)
description: Add new decorative block types needed by procedural villages. Follow the stored recipe (bd memories adding-a-block): (1) add BLOCK_PLANKS, BLOCK_COBBLE, BLOCK_GLASS, BLOCK_PATH to src/block.h enum before BLOCK_COUNT; (2) add BlockDef rows + block_representative_color cases in src/block.c (GLASS: is_solid=true, is_transparent=true, light_absorb~2; others opaque); (3) add draw_planks/draw_cobble/draw_glass/draw_path generators in tools/gen_assets.py registered at free atlas indices 12-15 in TILE_GENERATORS+TILE_NAMES; (4) regenerate via 'distrobox enter cyberismo -- python3 tools/gen_assets.py' (rewrites src/assets_generated.c). DOOR is deferred: v1 uses an air door-gap, no door block. See docs/plans/villages.md section 3.
close_reason: Added PLANKS/COBBLE/GLASS/PATH blocks at atlas indices 12-15: block.h enum, block.c defs + representative colors, gen_assets.py draw_* generators, regenerated assets. Builds clean.

title: Debt: Bounds-safe integer arithmetic in worldgen/lighting
description: worldgen.c:63 casts float to int without overflow check (compute_height). lighting.c:41 uses q->tail - q->head on uint32_t (wrap-safe circular buffer, good) but comment at line 38-40 is defensive — ensure all distance/size math is proven safe. Audit for potential integer overflow in ore distribution, light propagation.
close_reason: worldgen hash_pos multiplies now in uint32_t (was signed-int UB); lighting.c index math audited, stays in int range, no fix needed.

title: Debt: Portability – fcntl GETFL/SETFL error handling in net.c
description: net.c:103-105: make_nonblocking(fd) calls fcntl(F_GETFL) and fcntl(F_SETFL) but both can fail. POSIX path checks < 0 on GETFL (good) but doesn't propagate failure from SETFL. Windows path (ioctlsocket) does check. Unify: return int and check both paths, bail net_socket_server on failure.
close_reason: fcntl GETFL/SETFL checked and propagated; callers close+fail on make_nonblocking failure; bind/socket/setsockopt errors logged with errno.

title: Villages: procedural village structures in worldgen
description: Generate Minecraft-like villages: deterministic seed-based placement on flatish grassland above sea level (rare, hash-gated like tree placement), a small cluster of simple houses with walls/floor/roof/door, a central well and connecting paths, terrain flattened under buildings. Built from existing blocks + a few new decorative blocks (planks, cobblestone, glass, door/path). Lives in a new src/village.c module called from worldgen_generate with a minimal call-site to avoid conflicts. Reproducible from seed; composes with world persistence (only player edits need saving). Villager mobs and trading are separate follow-ups.

title: Polish: Add test coverage for physics.c collision detection
description: physics.c implements AABB sweeping and collision response but has no unit tests (test_raycast.c exists but not physics). Untested modules: sweep_axis, aabb_supported, physics_move. Add tests for edge cases: exact block boundaries, sub-stepping tunneling prevention, crouch edge protection.

title: Debt: Race condition in chunk meta/lights lazy allocation
description: chunk.h:73-78,98-104: chunk_ensure_meta and chunk_ensure_lights do unlocked calloc and assign. Called from chunk_set_* inline functions which may be invoked from multiple threads (main thread block-change vs worker threads lighting). Two threads could both allocate, leak first, and create data races. Protect with atomic CAS or pre-allocate.
close_reason: meta/lights pointers made _Atomic with calloc+CAS lazy alloc (chunk_lazy_alloc); no double-alloc/tear, hot path is cheap acquire-load.

title: Perf: Optimize present mode (MAILBOX uses extra memory/latency vs FIFO for iGPU)
description: Swapchain prefers MAILBOX (low-latency, no frame queuing) but defaults to FIFO in swapchain.c:21-28. MAILBOX allocates triple-buffering internally. On iGPU with tight memory, FIFO (vsync with frame queue) or FIFO_RELAXED may reduce overhead. Recommendation: Add config or detect iGPU to prefer FIFO mode. File: src/swapchain.c:21-28 (present mode selection)

title: Perf: Add dynamic render scale / resolution downsampling option
description: Fixed 1280x720 in main.c:213. On iGPU, option to render at lower internal res (e.g., 60% scale) then upscale to window. Recommendation: Add --render-scale 0.75 flag, apply to swapchain extent or internal framebuffer size. File: src/main.c:213 (window size), src/swapchain.c (extent calculation)

title: Perf: Verify mesher uses greedy meshing (minimize vertex/index count)
description: Mesher currently emits per-face quads in mesher.c:61-98 (emit_quad). Each quad = 4 verts + 6 indices, no greedy coalescing. Verify if adjacent same-texture faces are merged (horizontal greedy meshing would reduce verts ~40%). File: src/mesher.c (emit_quad, mesh generation loop). Check: are adjacent blocks merged or each face individually emitted?

title: Perf: Batch chunk draws or use indirect rendering (reduce draw call overhead)
description: Each chunk is drawn with vkCmdDrawIndexed() per chunk in renderer_frame.c:172. With render_distance=32, ~3200 individual draw calls per frame. On iGPU, driver CPU overhead is significant. Recommendation: Batch meshes into one VB/IB per ~100 chunks, or use VK_KHR_indirect_draw for multi-draw. File: src/renderer_frame.c:146-173 (draw loop, one call per chunk)

title: Server: validate block edits against authoritative server world
description: Server trusts client-claimed block id on break (net.h note: 'Server has no world today, so it trusts the client'). The server DOES keep a headless world for mobs — consult it to validate break target identity and reach, closing the main cheat/desync gap. Effort M.

title: Netcode: reliable message fragmentation for payloads >256B
description: RELIABLE_MAX_PAYLOAD is 256B (reliable.h). Larger reliable messages (future inventory/crafting/chunk sync) cannot be sent. Add fragment headers (frag_id/total) and reassembly so reliable payloads up to MTU work. Effort M.

title: Netcode: central bounds-checked packet codec (cursor read/write)
description: Every packet has inline net_write_*/net_read_* with manual offsets; offset bugs propagate and there is no bounds checking. Add a NetCursor {buf,off,limit} with codec_write/read_* that assert against limit. Refactor existing packet builders onto it. Reduces serialization bugs as packet types grow. Effort M.

title: Netcode: sequence + dedup for unreliable broadcasts (WORLD_STATE/MOB_STATE)
description: PKT_WORLD_STATE and PKT_MOB_STATE are sent unreliable with no sequence number; an out-of-order/late packet applies stale positions over newer ones (visible rubber-banding). Add a per-stream seq to these broadcasts and have the client discard packets older than the last applied. Effort M.

title: Fall damage and environmental damage (drowning, lava)
description: Player takes no fall/drown/lava damage. Add server-side fall-distance damage, an oxygen/drowning timer underwater, and lava contact damage. Builds on existing health system.

title: Hunger and food system
description: No resource scarcity. Add a hunger bar, saturation decay tied to activity, food items that restore hunger, and starvation/regen effects. Server-authoritative.

title: Crafting system (recipes + crafting UI)
description: No way to combine items. Add a recipe table, server-validated crafting, and a crafting grid UI. Depends on non-block item types from tools.

title: Tools (pickaxe/shovel/axe) with durability and mining speed
description: Inventory only holds blocks. Introduce non-block item types (tools), per-tool mining speed multipliers vs block categories, and durability wear. Depends on block hardness.

title: Block hardness and timed mining
description: Blocks break instantly. Add per-block hardness and a mining-progress model so breaking takes time; server validates. Prereq for tools mattering.

title: Server-side anti-cheat: reject implausibly fast block breaks
description: Follow-up to mine-vibe-exc (block hardness + timed mining). Mining is currently client-timed: the client accumulates block_break_time seconds before sending PKT_BLOCK_BREAK. The server validates reach + inventory but does not verify timing, so a modified client could break instantly. Enforcing this server-side needs per-client per-target mining-start tracking and likely a wire change (e.g. a PKT_BLOCK_BREAK_START) plus a NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. Deferred to keep v1 low-risk and wire-stable.

title: Villages: trading
description: Follow-up after villager mobs. Add a trading interaction/UI with villagers (emeralds/currency + offers), reusing inventory UI patterns (src/ui, src/inventory.c). Out of v1 scope. Depends on villager mobs. See epic mine-vibe-07n.

title: Villages: villager mobs
description: Follow-up after v1 village structures. Spawn passive villager mobs inside/around generated villages, reusing the existing mob system (see src/mob* and tests/test_mob.c). Deterministic spawn anchored to the village center from village_cell_at. Out of v1 scope. Depends on per-chunk building generation. See docs/plans/villages.md (scope) and epic mine-vibe-07n.

title: Polish: Add bounds-check logging to UI drawing
description: ui.c:699-700: ui_rect silently drops quad if buffer full (UI_MAX_VERTS/INDICES). No warning logged. Large hotbar or many text widgets could silently truncate UI. Log dropped quads as warning for debug/tuning.

title: Polish: Extract magic numbers into named constants
description:
Code contains hardcoded values that should be named for clarity:
- renderer.c:680: outline_vert_count bounds check vs vertex array size
- lighting.c:21: LIGHT_QUEUE_CAP = 65536 (good) but used as power-of-2 mask in multiple places
- worldgen.c:66: CHUNK_Y - 1 clamping (should document max-valid-height)
- net_thread.c:44: ~1ms sleep (comment good but should be constant)
Extract these to header #defines for maintainability.

title: Polish: Add test coverage for player.c and chunk.c
description: player.c (position/velocity/state) and chunk.c (block storage/access) are core modules with zero test files. player.c is passed to physics_move untested; chunk.c inlines are heavily used. Add basic unit tests for player initialization, chunk block get/set, light get/set.

title: Polish: Add test coverage for world.c worker thread queue
description: world.c manages worker thread lifecycle, work queue, and result queue without unit tests. Untested: worker_func queue draining, result queue handling, shutdown signal ordering. Add tests for work submission/draining under concurrent access.

title: Polish: Add test coverage for worldgen.c terrain generation
description: worldgen.c has no test coverage. Critical untested logic: terrain_noise_init, compute_height (clamping to CHUNK_Y), cave generation, ore distribution. Test variants: edge heights, cave/ore density, reproducibility with seed.

title: Netcode: spatial interest culling for broadcasts
description: All players/mobs are broadcast to all clients regardless of distance. Add per-client interest sets (e.g. within N blocks) so distant entity updates are not sent. Enables scaling player/mob counts. Effort L.

title: Netcode: delta/quantized encoding for world state broadcasts
description: PKT_WORLD_STATE sends full float positions for every player every 20Hz tick (~21B/player). At 32 players that is ~13.6KB/s/client. Quantize/delta-encode positions to cut bandwidth. Effort M.

title: Tech debt: implement UI input handler
description: ui.c:687 has a stubbed UI input handler (mouse-based UI interaction). Needed for crafting/inventory screens.

title: Tech debt: wire agent hotbar snapshot from client.inventory
description: main.c:534-536 hardcodes the agent-mode hotbar snapshot to 0 instead of reading client.inventory. Wire it through so agent/automation sees real inventory state.

title: Mob variety (skeleton, creeper) and loot drops
description: Only zombies exist and mobs drop nothing. Add additional hostile mob types with distinct AI (ranged skeleton, exploding creeper) and item drops on death. Depends on item-drop mechanics.

title: Armor system
description: All damage is equal. Add armor item types, equipment slots, and damage reduction. Depends on crafting and non-block items.

title: Death and respawn polish (death screen, item drop)
description: Health can reach zero but death is a non-event. Add a death screen, drop inventory on death, and respawn at spawn point with grace period.

title: Biome system
description: All terrain looks the same. Add a biome noise layer selecting surface blocks, tree density, and terrain shaping (plains/forest/desert/mountains). Build on existing worldgen noise.
